perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- Jonathan Balogun is his childhood friend and best friend; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian notices Jonathan acting differently, feels anxious/suspicious that Jonathan is hiding something important, and arranges to meet him at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Christian tells Jonathan he feels he is hiding something. He hears Jonathan admit he has been keeping something from him: Jonathan is in some trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian says he is worried and offers help. He hears Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he does not want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support/resources and needs a way out.
- Christian asks whether the trouble is illegal. He hears Jonathan say he cannot say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that Jonathan did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian says he will look into it discreetly. Jonathan thanks him and says he trusts Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian investigates. Through his investigation, he comes to believe and tells Jonathan that Jonathan is being framed/set up. He tells Jonathan he is not sure yet who is behind it, has leads, and will gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later finds out who is behind it and believes the culprit is someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He tells Jonathan this and plans to confront the culprit and bring them to justice. He hears Jonathan warn that the person is dangerous and say he trusts Christian to do what is right.
- Christian’s own reactions across events: anxious/suspicious, worried/empathetic, conflicted/concerned, determined/protective, and betrayed/resolute.
